Two days ago I unfortunately got a BSOD while gaming. To give a bit of background info, lately I've picked up the habit of listening to my podcasts in chrome minimized while I play various games. Well on this particular occasion I was listening to a podcast as usual while fiddling around with the resolution in the game I was in. I remember that every time I changed the resolution to a lower setting (for better performance) the game would just crash. In hindsight I should have taken that as a warning and moved on to something else but I have to admit I was a bit inebriated at the time and therefore stubborn; I wanted to game damnit. Anyway, the game crashed on me a solid three more times but the fourth time it crashed was the last straw for this pc. Now at this point I had been quite frustrated with the game's performance and decided to make a change in its launch settings. I removed the -dx81 from the settings after noticing that I should have removed that setting the first time I launched the game after installing an fpsconfig. I don't know if that had anything to do with it but I can't shake the feeling that maybe it did because as soon as I launched the game and opened up one of the options menus BOOM the audio of the podcast I was listening to in the background glitched the fuck out and my display went totally scrambled. Cut to blue screen. At that moment I was in total shock because this hadn't happened to me in about 3 years and as I said I was inebriated, so naturally I didn't take the short amount of time to read what the error was. I recall something along the lines of creating a memory dump or something but it was all just so fast. Then the screen went dark but the pc itself didn't turn off and I made a decision that I feel as though I should regret. Rather than waiting a few moments for the computer to shut itself off, I waited only a single moment and held the power button down a few seconds until it turned off. I thought to myself that maybe this will be just like the previous times this ole' bastard had blue screened and that everything would be fine once I rebooted. So I turned it on, chose start windows normally (like I've done the previous 3 times I've had a blue screen a few years ago), startup beep and splash screen, starting windows, log in to Steam and everything seems fine then I open chrome. I get the prompt that chrome was closed unexpectedly and was asked to restore my last session. I chose to restore and when my all my previous tabs opened up and tried to load, BSOD again. My heart sank and once again I was ignorant to the error and manually shut it down via the power button. Never had a BSOD twice in a row before...

I stood up and looked out my window, breathed a sigh of despair and cursed at the setting sun. Shit always seems to land on my lap when the night creeps in. But I digress. I sat my ass down and turned this bitch back on while doing everything the same as before. Logged in, opened chrome but chose not to restore the previous session and everything worked fine for the rest of the night. Though I didn't launch any games I just spent the rest of my time watching videos and browsing Voat. The next day (yesterday) was essentially an extension of the previous night in that I only spent my time browsing Voat and watching things. I also did some time doing research into the problem and that's when I began to lean more towards Chrome being the cause of this. Although the initial BSOD happened while I was constantly changing the resolution in a game, I did have chrome minimized with that podcast playing. The second time it happened only when I tried to do something in chrome. Thus I've come to the TDR (Timeout Detection & Recovery) problem. The information I retained of this issue mostly comes from this place and this other place. If anyone thinks that these issues are not similar to my case please let me know and I'll continue my research. Moving on, I finished yesterday without an issue and assumed that my problem might have taken care of itself somehow. But all it not as it seems because only today just an hour and a half ago I crashed again while multitasking in chrome. I wouldn't even call it multitasking, I just opened a youtube video while I was browsing Voat. But this time there was no blue screen only a frozen yet clearly glitched display. I say that because not only was the screen frozen (unable to move cursor and all) there were these little horizontal glitch slits maybe a pixel or two wide scattered about the display, and of course creepy audio glitching from the youtube video in accompaniment. It went like this for a good few seconds before I realized that maybe it's time to hit that power button again because clearly this system is frozen solid. Donk. So now I started back up in safe mode with networking so I could post this. Though my sound isn't working for some reason, chrome is behaving for now. I have nothing to do now but await answers.

Undercover marketers, PR people, or astroturfers. ("Astroturfing" is "fake grass roots," basically.)

These people pose as normal users, so that they can attempt to inject certain ideas, opinions, and viewpoints into the discussion. This could involve, for example, posting something positive about a product. It could also include seeding certain viewpoints in political discussions, or trying to dispel unpleasant opinions about a corporation.

The thing with Reddit and Voat is that they're not good places for direct advertising. They're designed for users to aggregate interesting content in an unbiased way, not for content marketers to promote products. However, Reddit (and to some extent, Voat) provides information that helps marketers to further laser-focus their audience targeting. For example, if you're advertising a brick-and-mortar video game store in Ontario, you could filter and display your ads to users whose subreddit subscriptions indicate that they both live in Ontario, and are interested in video gaming. This analytics potential does make Reddit (and to a less extent at this point, Voat) appealing for advertisers, but there isn't a lot of room on there for blatant ads. So many of us suspect that marketers (as well as possibly political lobbyists) may be posing as users to very subtly promote brands or even ideologies.
